title: BNP and NT-proBNP: Rule-Out Cut-Offs, Confounders and Sacubitril
summary: Learn how BNP and NT-proBNP are made and cleared, why 100 and 300 pg/mL are rule-out lines for acute heart failure rather than diagnoses, what age, kidney disease, obesity and sacubitril/valsartan do to the numbers, and why galectin-3 and sST2 are prognostic only.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 19 Hit 9 (BNP 100 / NT-proBNP 300), Hit 10 (neprilysin inhibitors; obesity and renal failure), Hit 14 (galectin-3 and ST2 prognostic) and Trap 3 (BNP on sacubitril/valsartan). Checked against Castiglione 2022, Meijers 2021 (HFA-ESC Biomarker Study Group) and Nishikimi 2022. Hit 9 says BNP 100 pg/mL “diagnoses” heart failure; the sources treat < 100 as a rule-out line with a 100–400 grey zone, and the lesson teaches that (register flag rv-bnp-100-rule-out). The NT-proBNP preference on sacubitril/valsartan is taught, with the qualification that the BNP rise is modest (register flag rv-arni-bnp-modest). Not taught: the reviewer’s NPV 89% and PPV 79% for BNP 100, the ~22-minute BNP half-life figure, week-to-week BNP variability; troponin, hs-CRP, D-dimer and homocysteine items.

objectives: Describe how BNP and NT-proBNP are produced and cleared, and why their values differ.
Apply acute and chronic heart failure rule-out cut-offs and recognise the grey zone.
Identify confounders, including obesity, kidney disease and sacubitril/valsartan, and choose the right peptide to monitor.
Distinguish prognostic markers (galectin-3, sST2) from diagnostic natriuretic peptides.

scenes.title: Three breathless patients
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three natriuretic peptide results arrive. (1) A 45-year-old with acute dyspnoea in the emergency department: BNP 140 pg/mL. (2) A 58-year-old with severe obesity and acute dyspnoea: BNP 80 pg/mL. (3) A patient with chronic heart failure two months after starting sacubitril/valsartan: BNP up from 220 to 260 pg/mL, NT-proBNP down. Question token: “Heart failure, ruled out, or getting worse?”

cues.text: Three natriuretic peptide results arrive: a breathless adult with a BNP of 140; a breathless patient with severe obesity and a BNP of 80; and a heart failure patient whose BNP rose after starting sacubitril and valsartan.
In the third patient, the NT-proBNP fell over the same two months.
Is each result heart failure, a rule-out, or a patient getting worse?

props.label: Heart failure, ruled out, or worse?

scenes.title: One precursor, two peptides
scenes.altText: Schematic: a stretched ventricular myocyte releases proBNP, which is cleaved into active BNP and inactive NT-proBNP. Clearance cards: BNP is removed by binding to the NPR-C receptor, by neprilysin degradation and about 25% unchanged by the kidneys; NT-proBNP is cleared only passively, mainly by the kidney. Half-life card: NT-proBNP about 120 minutes vs BNP about 20 minutes, with NT-proBNP concentrations about 6 times higher.

cues.text: Volume overload and stretch make heart muscle cells release a precursor, proBNP. It is split into two pieces: active BNP and an inactive fragment, NT-proBNP.
BNP is cleared three ways: by a clearance receptor, by the enzyme neprilysin, and about a quarter unchanged in urine.
NT-proBNP has no active clearance. It is removed passively, mainly by the kidney.
So NT-proBNP lasts longer, about 120 minutes against about 20 for BNP, and circulates at roughly six times the concentration. The two are not interchangeable numbers.

props.label: Half-life ~120 min vs ~20 min · NT-proBNP ~6× higher

scenes.title: Rule-out first, grey zone second
scenes.altText: Acute heart failure cut-off card (ESC position paper values as summarised by Castiglione 2022; ng/L = pg/mL): BNP < 100 unlikely, 100–400 grey zone, > 400 likely. NT-proBNP < 300 unlikely at any age; rule-in > 450 (age < 50), > 900 (50–75), > 1800 (> 75). Evidence card: Breathing Not Properly, 1586 dyspnoeic ED patients, BNP 100 ng/L — sensitivity 90%, specificity 76%, accuracy 83%; PRIDE, NT-proBNP < 300 ng/L — negative predictive value 99%. Chronic heart failure card: BNP < 35 and NT-proBNP < 125 ng/L make heart failure unlikely.

cues.text: In acute breathlessness, the natriuretic peptides are best at ruling out. A BNP below 100, or an NT-proBNP below 300, makes acute heart failure unlikely.
Above those lines is not a diagnosis. BNP from 100 to 400 is a grey zone; above 400, heart failure is likely. NT-proBNP rule-in values climb with age: 450, 900 and 1800.

The evidence: in the Breathing Not Properly study of 1586 patients, a BNP of 100 was 90 percent sensitive but only 76 percent specific. In PRIDE, an NT-proBNP below 300 had a 99 percent negative predictive value.
Outside the acute setting the bar is lower: BNP below 35 or NT-proBNP below 125 makes chronic heart failure unlikely. Higher values still need further investigation to confirm.

scenes.title: What pushes the number around
scenes.altText: Confounder cards. Raise natriuretic peptides: advanced age, kidney disease, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute coronary syndrome, sepsis. Lower them: obesity (50% lower cut-offs proposed). Sacubitril/valsartan card: neprilysin inhibition raises BNP (median +19% at 8–10 weeks in PARADIGM-HF) while NT-proBNP falls (median −28%); NT-proBNP is the marker of choice, though some authors argue BNP stays usable because the rise is modest. Hook answers: (1) BNP 140 is in the grey zone — not a diagnosis; image and assess; (2) obesity lowers peptides, so a BNP of 80 does not exclude heart failure as reliably; (3) follow NT-proBNP, which is falling.

cues.text: Read every value in context. Age, kidney disease, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute coronary syndrome and sepsis all raise natriuretic peptides.
Obesity lowers them, with or without heart failure, so cut-offs about half as high have been proposed in obese patients.
Sacubitril blocks neprilysin. In PARADIGM-HF, median BNP rose 19 percent while NT-proBNP fell 28 percent, so NT-proBNP is the marker of choice on this drug.
Back to the hook. A BNP of 140 is grey zone, not a diagnosis. A BNP of 80 with severe obesity is a weaker rule-out. And on sacubitril, the falling NT-proBNP is the trend to trust.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “BNP ≥ 100 confirms heart failure” (✓ 100 is a rule-out line; 100–400 is a grey zone); “On sacubitril, a rising BNP means worsening” (✓ neprilysin inhibition raises BNP; follow NT-proBNP); “Galectin-3 or sST2 diagnoses heart failure” (✓ prognostic only; neither is cardiac-specific).

cues.text: Trap one: a BNP of 100 or more confirms heart failure. No: 100 is a rule-out line, and up to 400 is a grey zone.
Trap two: on sacubitril, a rising BNP means the heart is failing. No: the drug slows BNP breakdown. Follow NT-proBNP.
Trap three: galectin-3 or soluble ST2 diagnoses heart failure. No: neither is cardiac-specific. They predict outcome; they do not diagnose.

scenes.title: Doorman, witness, fortune teller
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “BNP and NT-proBNP are DOORMEN: below 100 or 300 they turn heart failure away, above it they only let it into the waiting room. On sacubitril, NT-proBNP is the honest WITNESS because neprilysin does not break it down. Galectin-3 and sST2 are FORTUNE TELLERS: they predict the future, not the diagnosis.” Tokens: doorman = BNP/NT-proBNP rule-out · witness = NT-proBNP on sacubitril · fortune teller = galectin-3/sST2. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the natriuretic peptides are doormen. Below 100 or 300 they turn heart failure away; above, they only let it into the waiting room. On sacubitril, NT-proBNP is the honest witness. Galectin-3 and soluble ST2 are fortune tellers: they predict, they do not diagnose.

Where it breaks: the doorman’s line moves with age, kidney function and obesity; BNP and NT-proBNP assays and cut-offs are not interchangeable; and the BNP rise on sacubitril is modest, so some experts still use BNP.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “BNP < 100 · NT-proBNP < 300 → acute HF unlikely; above = grey zone, not diagnosis”, “Age, kidney ↑ · obesity ↓ · sacubitril → follow NT-proBNP · galectin-3/sST2 = prognosis”.

cues.text: Use a BNP below 100 or an NT-proBNP below 300 picograms per millilitre to argue against acute heart failure, read higher values in the light of age, kidney function and obesity, follow NT-proBNP on sacubitril and valsartan, and treat galectin-3 and soluble ST2 as prognostic rather than diagnostic markers.

props.label: BNP < 100 · NT-proBNP < 300 → acute HF unlikely; above = grey zone
Age, kidney ↑ · obesity ↓ · sacubitril → NT-proBNP · Gal-3/sST2 = prognosis

explanation.what: Plain language: a stretched, overloaded heart releases a hormone precursor that splits into BNP and a leftover fragment, NT-proBNP. Low levels make heart failure unlikely; high levels raise suspicion but do not prove it. Scientific terms: proBNP, BNP (active), NT-proBNP (inactive), NPR-C clearance receptor, neprilysin, angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI; sacubitril/valsartan), negative predictive value, grey zone, galectin-3, soluble ST2 (sST2).
explanation.why: The peptides have high sensitivity and negative predictive value but modest specificity, because many non-heart-failure conditions raise them. BNP is actively degraded (partly by neprilysin), while NT-proBNP is cleared passively by the kidney, so drugs and kidney function affect the two differently.
explanation.measure: Acute HF unlikely: BNP < 100 ng/L (pg/mL), NT-proBNP < 300 ng/L. Grey zone BNP 100–400; HF likely > 400; NT-proBNP rule-in 450 (< 50 y), 900 (50–75 y), 1800 (> 75 y). Chronic HF unlikely: BNP < 35, NT-proBNP < 125. Breathing Not Properly: BNP 100, sensitivity 90%, specificity 76%. PRIDE: NT-proBNP < 300, NPV 99%. Obesity: about 50% lower cut-offs proposed. PARADIGM-HF: BNP median +19%, NT-proBNP median −28% at 8–10 weeks.
explanation.differs: BNP (active, half-life ~20 min, neprilysin substrate) vs NT-proBNP (inactive, ~120 min, renal, not a neprilysin substrate); rule-out vs rule-in thresholds; diagnostic natriuretic peptides vs prognostic galectin-3 and sST2.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: pick which peptide to monitor on sacubitril/valsartan, interpret a BNP just above 100, recognise obesity as lowering and kidney disease as raising the peptides, or identify galectin-3/sST2 as prognostic markers.

mnemonic.text: BNP and NT-proBNP are DOORMEN: below 100 or 300 they turn heart failure away, above it they only let it into the waiting room. On sacubitril, NT-proBNP is the honest WITNESS because neprilysin does not break it down. Galectin-3 and sST2 are FORTUNE TELLERS: they predict the future, not the diagnosis.
mnemonic.explanation: Separates rule-out use, drug-proof monitoring and prognosis.
mnemonic.limitation: Cut-offs shift with age, kidney function and obesity; BNP and NT-proBNP assays and cut-offs are not interchangeable; the BNP rise on sacubitril is modest and some experts still use BNP.

Cut-off values are the ESC position-paper values as summarised in one review; local guidelines and assays differ.
takeaway: Use a BNP below 100 or an NT-proBNP below 300 picograms per millilitre to argue against acute heart failure, read higher values in the light of age, kidney function and obesity, follow NT-proBNP on sacubitril and valsartan, and treat galectin-3 and soluble ST2 as prognostic rather than diagnostic markers.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic heart failure starts sacubitril/valsartan. Eight weeks later he feels better; BNP has risen modestly and NT-proBNP has fallen. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Follow NT-proBNP; neprilysin inhibition slows BNP breakdown, so the falling NT-proBNP reflects improvement
options.rationale: Correct. Neprilysin degrades BNP but not NT-proBNP; on sacubitril/valsartan BNP tends to rise while NT-proBNP falls, so NT-proBNP is the marker of choice.

options.text: Heart failure is worsening because BNP has risen
options.rationale: Incorrect. The BNP rise is expected from reduced neprilysin degradation and does not by itself mean worsening.

options.text: The NT-proBNP fall is an assay error because both peptides come from the same precursor
options.rationale: Incorrect. They share a precursor but are cleared differently, so they can move in opposite directions on this drug.
Incorrect. Galectin-3 is a prognostic marker, not cardiac-specific, and is not a substitute for natriuretic peptides.

questions.stem: In a non-obese 45-year-old with acute dyspnoea, which result best argues against acute heart failure?

options.rationale: Correct. NT-proBNP below 300 pg/mL makes acute heart failure unlikely; in PRIDE this cut-off had a 99% negative predictive value.
Incorrect. This is in the 100–400 grey zone: it neither rules in nor rules out.
Incorrect. BNP above 400 pg/mL makes heart failure likely.
Incorrect. Above 450 pg/mL in a patient under 50, heart failure is likely.

questions.stem: Which statement about natriuretic peptide confounders is correct?

options.text: Obesity lowers BNP and NT-proBNP, so a normal value is a weaker rule-out in obese patients
options.rationale: Correct. Natriuretic peptides are lower in obese people with or without heart failure; lower cut-offs have been proposed.

options.text: Kidney disease lowers NT-proBNP because the kidney produces it
options.rationale: Incorrect. NT-proBNP is made by cardiac myocytes and cleared mainly by the kidney, so kidney disease raises it.
Incorrect. Levels rise with age, which is why NT-proBNP rule-in cut-offs are age-stratified.
Incorrect. Arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation raise natriuretic peptides.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 19 Hit 9 says BNP 100 pg/mL “diagnoses” heart failure in acute dyspnoea. Castiglione 2022 (ESC values) treats BNP < 100 ng/L as making acute HF unlikely, 100–400 as a grey zone and > 400 as likely, and notes higher values need further investigation to confirm. The lesson teaches 100 as a rule-out line (register flag rv-bnp-100-rule-out).

Ch. 19 Hit 10, Trap 3 and the memory hook say NT-proBNP is the only honest marker on sacubitril. Castiglione 2022 supports NT-proBNP as the biomarker of choice, but Nishikimi 2022 reports the BNP rise is modest (PARADIGM-HF median +19%) and argues BNP remains usable. The lesson teaches NT-proBNP preference with this qualification (register flag rv-arni-bnp-modest).
